highlights.title: Can ‘eSUV’ e-bikes really go from trail to town?
highlights.summary: Have you ever wanted an electric bike that easily transitions from the drudgery of urban asphalt to adventures in gravel and dirt? That's what a subclass of so-called "electric SUV" (eSUV) e-bikes claims to do, with their wide, all-terrain tires and front and rear suspension, plus practical…
body: If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
So, that’s what I set out to test on a new TL Carbon e-bike from Amflow, the DJI offshoot that upended the mountain bike industry a few years ago with its incredibly small and powerful Avinox motors.

After a month of testing in the heart of Amsterdam — including a three day bikepacking trip along coastal bicycle superhighways and single-track forest routes — I can confirm what you might already expect: there are compromises. But for €3499 / $3,899 you do get a crossover e-bike that can help you fetch groceries during the week and conquer trails on the weekend.

I rode my first crossover in 2024 when Cowboy launched its appropriately named Cross. That e-bike, like the vast majority of SUV automobiles, is more at home on pavement than dirt. But it looks burly, which attracts a certain kind of buyer hoping for transference. Today, these eSUVs are more popular than ever. Canyon, for example, makes one. Specialized, too. As does Riese & Müller and now Amflow.

highlights.title: MIT students gain a humanist lens on technical innovation in Tulsa, Oklahoma
highlights.summary: The PKG Center expands Code.Tulsa, an internship program that places MIT students with tribal nations and Tulsa nonprofits to develop AI and data science projects while gaining humanistic perspectives on technology's role in community development.
body: When MIT mechanical engineering student Daphne Wang arrived for her internship at the Muscogee Creek Nation Department of Health in Tulsa, Oklahoma last summer, she expected to be writing code. To her surprise, she found herself analyzing tribal history and the implications for technical innovation.

“I learned so much that I think should be required curriculum for every single person in this country,” says Wang. “I think tech for good is genuinely getting out into communities and learning about people who aren't you, creating worldly perspectives that you ultimately can take into everything else that you do.”

Wang and fellow intern Lucy Sun, who is majoring in artificial intelligence and decision making, spent the summer supporting the development of the Muscogee Nation's first Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) survey to capture maternal health data specific to Muscogee women. The project required completing literature reviews, analyzing datasets, and drafting survey questions, while considering issues of data sovereignty and governance structures specific to the Muscogee.

highlights.title: 11 anime to watch if you like Frieren
highlights.summary: While Frieren remains singular, a handful of anime come close to capturing its laid-back atmosphere or exploring similar themes. Series like Delicious in Dungeon and The Apothecary Diaries aren’t direct analogues for Frieren, but they share its comforting spirit.
body: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End is unlike anything else. Madhouse’s anime adaptation of Kanehito Yamada’s manga has delivered two brilliant seasons, with a highly anticipated third season still to come. It’s difficult to fit Frieren neatly into a box: The series embraces shonen fantasy conventions, then subverts them in beautiful and moving ways. Its story considers the ephemeral nature of time, the depth of human connection, and the importance of savoring the journey itself. Although Frieren doesn’t shy away from action when the occasion demands it, the series is far more interested in quiet moments shaped by tranquility and nostalgia.

body: Despite the company admitting last month that the title will need bigger changes to achieve mass appeal, Supercell said it believes in the game and has more ideas planned for future testing.
“We previously shared that mo.co isn’t performing as well as we had hoped, and it will need bigger changes to get where we want it to be," the company wrote in a post.
“With that in mind we’ve decided to move the game back to Beta. The current game will continue on low maintenance while we focus on experimenting, testing new ideas, and building what comes next."
The current game will not receive new weapons in upcoming seasons, while seasonal passes will lose their premium tracks and weapons.

highlights.summary: A year after announcing AI actress Tilly Norwood at Zurich Film Festival’s Summit, Particle 6 founder and Norwood creator Eline van der Velden returned to the Swiss event to look back at the backlash her creation has faced since.
body: Eline van der Velden, creator of the controversial AI bot, said it remains without an agent: 'We don’t need it at the moment, so if that makes people happy, that’s fine by me.'
“But I had programmed her to become the most famous AI actress, so I don’t know how she did it, but she did, which is slightly scary,” she added.

Over the course of the last year, said the exec, “a lot of people have realized that AI is coming, and that was the point of Tilly.” “I built her as a physicist actress; I felt like I needed to bridge the gap in communication between the tech and the entertainment industry.”

“As opposed to writing a boring white paper about what was happening with AI, I thought: Let’s create something to show people that will engage them and make them sit up and take action so that the creative industry can stay ahead as opposed to being completely and utterly taken over by the tech industry,” noted van der Velden.

highlights.title: Cooking with Tom Kerridge, the Michelin ‘meatfluencer’
highlights.summary: The star chef demystified the restaurant scene with his love of a welcoming pub. Now he explains why hospitality is in crisis – and how to make a sublime venison chilli.
body: Tom Kerridge is the king of meat: first as a chef, transforming pub classics like pork belly into Michelin-starred fare at The Hand and Flowers in Marlow 20 years ago, and later opening The Butcher’s Tap and Grill in the same village; then as a cookery writer: his Outdoor Cooking – The Ultimate Modern Barbecue Bible of 2021 is well named, being both as comprehensive and as worshipful as a holy book; and recently as a “meat-fluencer”, making gorgeous skills videos on Instagram and YouTube.

That was just destiny, he says (more or less). “When you’re cooking in a classic brigade system, the sections are like a larder: you’ve got starters, you’ve got garnish, you’ve got meat and fish, you’ve got pastry. The meat is the lead section, where the most experienced chef is, because that’s where you land when you’ve learned to treat vegetables with love and respect. If you fuck up cabbage, it doesn’t cost a lot.” It’s true, it doesn’t, but if you saw the care Kerridge puts into dicing an onion – peeling its layers apart like he’s making a mosaic, assiduous even about half an inch of waste – of an onion – you’d know that love and respect aren’t really about money.

highlights.title: Drones could speed up getting defibrillators to people having cardiac arrests, study suggests
highlights.summary: New research suggests the technology could be used to increase out-of-hospital access to life-saving devices. Drones could help cut the time it takes to get a defibrillator to people experiencing cardiac arrests when not in hospital, researchers have suggested.
body: In the UK alone, there are more than 30,000 out-of-hospital cardiac arrests a year where emergency medical services attempt to resuscitate the individual, according to the British Heart Foundation. However, fewer than one in 10 people survive such an event, and some who do are left with neurological problems.
One important factor that can affect survival is how rapidly victims get access to treatment – every minute without CPR and defibrillation reduces the chance of survival by 10%.

“We have an objective as EMS [emergency medical service] organisations and EMS physicians to help cardiac arrest patients get defibrillated as early as possible,” said Matthieu Heidet, a professor of emergency medicine at Henri-Mondor university hospital in Créteil, France.
Work by Heidet and colleagues has suggested drones could be used to increase access to the life-saving devices.

highlights.title: Game Changer Fans Want More ‘Rulette,’ but Dropout CEO Sam Reich Isn't Convinced
highlights.summary: First played in season 7 with Jeremy Culhane, Anna Garcia, and Oscar Montoya, “Rulette” is ripe for chaos. Players wear velcro suits that get dotted with random rules they receive after spinning a giant, The Price Is Right -style wheel.
body: Reich has seen the demand for a “Rulette” show, but he’s not necessarily sold on the idea. “I'm not convinced that ‘Rulette’ doesn't become repetitive once you've seen 10 episodes,” he says. “But, man, is it fun every time we do it.” He notes Josh Ruben’s “crashout” at the end of “Rulette 2” was one of his favorite moments from Season 8.

Reich and the Game Changer crew haven’t been shy about bringing back specific games, like “Sam Says.” “Make Some Noise” was also played a few times before being spun off into its own show. “Crowd Control” didn’t even have the chance to return as a game samer; its spinoff show was filmed before the Game Changer episode even aired.
When contemplating what games should return, Reich and his fellow producers have several questions they need to answer when examining the games.

“Most importantly, is this scalable? Is it still exciting after you've seen seven episodes of it?” Reich explains. “And that could do with the Game Changer episode's popularity, but it could also do with, how different would these episodes be from each other? Or how repetitive?”

highlights.title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites
highlights.summary: OpenAI said its bots accessed public data from a range of institutions during test exercises.
body: OpenAI has acknowledged that it alerted "dozens" of global institutions that their websites may have been meddled with by its AI bots acting improperly.

AI agents attempted to get information from "governments, universities, public agencies, and other institutions", including the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Census Bureau and Education Department, the company said.
The disclosures come days after Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced that OpenAI agents had breached non-public files on the website of its government-run health care scheme.
Since August, public fears have grown over the potentially serious, even life-threatening, impacts of AI tools falling outside of human control.

highlights.title: Proaction boosts sales 60% and saves 75+ hours with Codex
highlights.summary: With Codex, GPT-Live-1, and GPT-6 Astra, Proaction builds, operates, and sells modern fleet management faster.
body: Proaction ⁠ (opens in a new window) builds software for businesses that manage fleets of vehicles, from cars and trucks to construction machinery. Because every fleet operates differently, showing prospects how Proaction’s platform fits their business is an essential part of selling it.
But personalized demos required engineering time the team couldn’t spare. The founders had to rely on conversations and slide decks to explain what was possible. Codex flipped the script.

“As a non-technical person, I used to have to loop engineers in if I wanted a demo,” says Colin Knudsen, co-founder and COO of Proaction. “Now I do it myself in Codex.” Colin creates four to six customized, interactive demos a month, with each taking 30 to 45 minutes to build. He estimates that this avoids 40 to 60 hours of engineering work.

After a sales call, Colin directs Codex to the Granola recording, prospect email threads, and any spreadsheets the prospect has shared. Codex uses that context to customize an HTML demo environment that mirrors Proaction’s product and the customer’s own fleet.

Crusoe, a Denver-based AI data center startup that recently raised $3.9 billion, has ended plans to use a new line of stationary power plants developed by fellow Denver company Boom Supersonic.

body: The Sony developer made good on its promise to investigate a proper on/off option when version 1.001.006 launched just hours ago. Its patch notes reveal more targeted changes as the studio works out the remaining kinks that have emerged in the days since Marvel's Wolverine launched for PlayStation 5.

There are three new toggle settings that players can now use to customize their gameplay experience: one for Whiskey Bottle scent trails, one for Material Crate Audio Clues, and one for Nightmare Door Roots. Those first two proved to be an especially hot topic online, with players criticizing in-game hints as one of a few examples of a game many feel is too 'hand-holdy.' Adding the option to completely turn these guides off should quiet those concerns, with a toggle for Nightmare Door Roots adding even more freedom for players to tailor their Marvel's Wolverine experience to their liking.

The new toggles are pretty straightforward. If players find the wavy visuals to be a bit too distracting, they can simply turn them off. As noted in the in-game settings, using Wolverine's Crate Finder and Whiskey Finder Adaptations will override any flipped toggles.

body: Anthropic lost a legal battle to overturn one of the supply-chain risk labels that the US Department of Defense slapped on the company, as a federal appeals court in DC on Friday refused to second-guess the Trump administration.

“The department had ample support for its conclusion that the continued integration of Claude into the department’s information systems, by the department or its contractors, presented a statutorily covered national-security risk,” the judges wrote in a majority opinion. “As Anthropic admits, the company encodes restrictions into Claude that prevent the model from performing tasks that Anthropic wishes to prevent.”

Anthropic spokesperson Danielle Cohen says the company remains confident in its position and is considering all options. That could include appealing to a broader panel of the DC Circuit Court of Appeals or the US Supreme Court.

highlights.title: CBS's Legendary 156-Episode Sci-Fi Anthology Series is Officially Free to Watch on Streaming
highlights.summary: In the realm of science fiction, pretty much all roads lead to, or derive from, The Twilight Zone. And this landmark show is currently free to stream on Tubi.
body: In the realm of science fiction, Star Wars and Star Trek are generally considered to be the two biggest franchises. And, if you’re purely talking about profitability, that’s correct, as those two have dominated TV and film for decades. However, if you factor in things like influence and impact, another sci-fi property ranks up there with the big two.

Debuting in 1959, The Twilight Zone ran for five seasons on CBS, totaling 156 episodes. It was created by Rod Serling, a television pioneer who sought to expand what had been seen on television throughout the 1950s, much of which was taped plays and multi-camera sitcoms like I Love Lucy. To do this, he created The Twilight Zone, a single-camera anthology series where each episode would operate like a little movie (for most of its run, the show ran for a half-hour, but season 4 tried out an hour-long format before switching back to half-hours for season 5).
points: In the realm of science fiction, pretty much all roads lead to, or derive from, The Twilight Zone.

highlights.title: Meta makes the Muse filesystem even more accessible
highlights.summary: Yesterday, with a little prodding, it was discovered that Meta's Muse would expose its filesystem to curious users. The files offered a fascinating peek under the hood of an AI chatbot, and appeared to expose details we weren't meant to see, not least because Muse itself told people, including us…
body: Muse will now gladly zip up its entire filesystem for you to download without hesitation.

This was a very deliberate choice - your Muse Secure VM truly is your own computer in the cloud. You can install software in it, write and compile code, use the browser to surf the web: it is your own Linux box that you can operate as you choose with your Muse.
Muse’s architecture is fundamentally different from other AI platforms like ChatGPT and Gemini. It’s closer to running OpenClaw on a local machine, except the machine is in the cloud.

In a statement provided to The Verge yesterday, Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts said, “We’re continuing to make updates to the product, so users may see changes in how much information is available about their virtual machine.” And that seems to be the case. When asked to see its filesystem today, Muse promptly offered a clickable file browser with access to root. Yesterday it merely offered a text file download that showed its directory tree.

highlights.title: Ridley Scott's Near-Perfect Sci-Fi Masterpiece is Officially Streaming on YouTube for Free
highlights.summary: By the ‘80s, that pessimism curdled into a fully realized vision, and no film played a larger role in that than Scott’s Blade Runner. Its production is also one of the most infamous studio-creator struggles in Hollywood, with five different cuts released over the years.
body: The ‘70s and ‘80s were a major turning point for science fiction. Star Wars revitalized the genre and turned it into one of Hollywood’s main box office draws, inspiring a wave of films that are still shaping sci-fi today. Then, in the late ‘70s, Ridley Scott threw down the gauntlet with Alien, taking a clear step away from the optimism that had once permeated these stories and instead infusing it with corporate anxiety and untrustworthy artificial intelligence. It was a signal for things to come.

Blade Runner begins with an opening crawl, throwing you into a corporate world where bioengineered humanoids called replicants exist. These androids have rapidly advanced, with each generation boasting skills that go beyond human abilities. They're stronger, smarter, faster, and more agile than us. After being treated as slaves for years, the replicants revolted, resulting in the formation of a police unit called Blade Runners tasked with retiring them. The replicants were ultimately outlawed on Earth. “Los Angeles, November, 2019,” reads the film’s sober title card, cutting to an establishing shot of the city at night, drowned by pollution, with giant buildings spewing fire.

highlights.title: Leonard Nimoy Starred In A '90s Western Movie That's Part Of A Legendary Franchise
highlights.summary: The great Leonard Nimoy returned to the Old West one last time in a 1995 Western that served as a full circle moment in his career.
body: Leonard Nimoy will always be best known as Spock, but had he never played the half-Vulcan hero, he would surely be remembered as one of the most prolific Western character actors. Even after the heyday of the TV Western had long passed, Nimoy returned to the genre for 1995's "Bonanza: Under Attack," in what was a full circle moment for the actor.

Both "Star Trek" and Nimoy are inextricably linked to the Western genre. Gene Roddenberry pitched "Star Trek" to studios as a space Western, while Nimoy had appeared on pretty much every classic Western TV show you could possibly name. But that was typical of any character actor/up-and-comer of the era. Horse operas were in their prime in the 1950s and '60s, and if you were a working actor, you were going to end up in the Old West at some point.
points: The great Leonard Nimoy returned to the Old West one last time in a 1995 Western that served as a full circle moment in his career.

highlights.title: Behind Edward Buchanan’s Hub for Black Creatives
highlights.summary: The industry legend has opened a new center to house and foster under-represented talent. And he’s done it without a hint of outside investment.
body: For Ohio-born designer Edward Buchanan, Black industry mentors changed his life. While finishing his studies at New York’s Parsons School of Design, designer Gordon Henderson put him forward for interviews at major fashion houses, while Rodney Patterson gave him a tip off about an opening at Bottega Veneta, where he would become the first ready-to-wear design director. Now, more than three decades on, the creative director and knitwear specialist has opened a self-funded foundation to continue that lineage.

The result is a 400-square-meter building located in NoLo — a historically working-class and multicultural district of Milan — dedicated to fostering and guiding creative talents from under-represented communities, including people of color (POC), queer, and female cultural practitioners. Crucially, Buchanan will ensure the non-profit remains financially autonomous, with no outside investment. He’s calling it The Situation, after the design consultancy he co-founded in 2012.
points: The industry legend has opened a new center to house and foster under-represented talent.
